item.title: GAS: Domestic market gets 41.3% as Nigeria’s supply averages 4.95bcf/d in 10 months
item.description: •LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM By Udeme Akpan Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d), representing 41.3 per cent of the country’s total supply of 4.95 bcf/d in the first 10 months of 2026. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest report obtained by Vanguard. The report showed that the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, received the remaining 58.7 per cent, averaging 2.91 bcf/d. In October, total average daily gas supply rose by 2.7 per cent to 4.951 bcf/d, from 4.822 bcf/d in September. Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d. April recorded the highest average daily supply during the 10-month period at 5.141 bcf/d, comprising 2.01 bcf/d for domestic market and 3.13 bcf/d for NLNG. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Supply to the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids facility fell by two per cent. Gas exports also strengthened. Average daily LNG exports increased by seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, from 49,198 metric tonnes per day in September, while pipeline exports through the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) rose by 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d, from 0.134 bcf/d. LPG retail price rises 12.5% to ₦1,800 per kg Meanwhile, the average retail price of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, also known as cooking gas, rose by 12.5 per cent to ₦1,800 per kilogramme in November 2026, from ₦1,600 in October. Checks by Vanguard attributed the increase largely to limited supply. The average depot price of LPG stood at ₦1,274 in the Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, November 20, 2026. The report covered Lagos, Warri, Calabar and Port Harcourt but did not provide a regional breakdown of LPG prices. Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Bassey Essien, told Vanguard in an interview that Nigeria must make its domestic gas market commercially attractive to secure adequate supplies. He said: “Gas exports generate foreign exchange, but the domestic market must also be commercially attractive enough to secure adequate supply. ‘’The solution is not to stop exports but to make the domestic market competitive enough to attract supply while preserving export earnings.” On Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, Essien noted that regulation alone could not guarantee physical deliveries without adequate infrastructure and effective payment systems. “The Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, requires producers to supply the local marke

item.title: President Tinubu does not need this falsehood
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abundant evidence, provided by Tinubu himself, to call that assertion a deliberate lie. I have touched on some of them before; but, Tinubu, despite expert advice continues to campaign on a promise which can never be redeemed. Here again, the facts which Tinubu stubbornly ignores; because they don’t fit into the narratives of a desperate politician running for elections, will once more be presented. This time fresh evidence will be added from Tinubu’s campaign organization. POLITICS AND FALSEHOOD ARE INSEPRABLE “The great masses of the people ..will fall victims to a great lie than to a small one.” Adolf Hitler, 1899-1945, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS, VBQ p 130. Politicians, under the best of circumstances, would repeat the same falsehood in the hope that saying it long enough will make it true. And, when they fail, they never apologise to the people; they blame others. President Tinubu’s assertion that Nigeria’s economy can grow to $1 trillion by 2030 is the sort of thing Hitler was talking about. I have given Tinubu the benefit of doubt that he read accounting in an American university as an undergraduate. But, his insistence that the Nigerian economy, whose Gross Domestic Product, GDP, is estimated to reach $386.67 billion at the end of the year 2026 could reach $1 trillion in just four years, would have had first year students of any university wondering if that was a joke or something else not hilarious. The figures don’t add up. LIARS CAN FIGURE; FIGURES DON’T LIE “Every government is run by liars and nothing they say should be believed. I.F Stone, 1907-1989. US Journalist and Publisher. Stone was one of my favourite columnists during my ten years in the US. I read his articles as if preparing for an examination on the subject discussed. He always led with evidence. So, let us start with the Federal Governments own figures. President Tinubu has been going round the country telling Nigerians the Nigerian economy is set to grow by 4.5 per cent this year. That will be the best performance since 2014. It is admittedly very commendable but worse than Jonathan’s worst year. The FG is also promising 6 percent growth in 2027. Highly praise-worthy if achieved. For some reason, not too difficult to understand, Tinubu, a self-proclaimed accountant, as well as his mob of supporters, cannot seem to understand that you cannot grow $386.67 billion to $1 trillion at 6 per cent in four years. This is primary school arithmetic called compound interest calculations. It is repeated at freshman level in American universities. item.title: How Oyibo, BEDC worker was murdered 4 months into marriage
item.description: •Disco, Delta community mourn •Family shattered, seeks justice By Egufe Yafugborhi & Cynthia Alo Oscar Eze, popularly known as Oyibo or NEPA Man, left home on Monday, November 16, 2026, for another routine assignment as an operations personnel of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company, BEDC, Agbor Business Unit. The 38-year-old had no reason to suspect that the day’s work in Umunede, Ika North-East Local Government Area of Delta State, would be his last. Four months after remarrying following the death of his first wife, Eze was brutally murdered in circumstances that have left his pregnant wife, young son and elderly mother devastated, while colleagues and residents mourn a man widely remembered for his cheerful disposition. His last assignment took him to a relatively isolated suburb of Idumu-Oba, with sparsely distributed buildings. While working alongside other workmen at a property apparently undergoing finishing, he was ambushed by a gang of youths. A CCTV camera at the premises captured the horrifying encounter. The assailants accosted him around the small entrance gate, dragged him into the compound and repeatedly stabbed him with daggers as other workmen watched in fear. He sustained multiple injuries to his upper body and died shortly afterwards. He was rushed to hospital, where he was confirmed dead. The police subsequently confirmed that Eze was attacked on November 16, at about 1.15 p.m., during a power disconnection exercise at Ileje Quarters, Umunede. According to BEDC management, the property he had disconnected owed the company almost N300,000 in electricity bills. His attackers allegedly trailed him after the disconnection. A legitimate assignment to earn a living ended in a gruesome killing, leaving a community asking how a familiar electricity worker could have become the target of such violence. A young marriage shattered Beyond the circumstances of his death lies the tragedy of a family whose hopes have been abruptly shattered. Eze’s first wife died about two years ago, leaving him with a son. He subsequently remarried barely four months before his death. His new wife was reportedly pregnant. A neighbour close to the BEDC office affirmed: “His first wife, who had a child for him, died about two years ago. Then he remarried four months ago. “I don’t know where the new wife is from. His former wife was from here (Umunede). Oyibo lived at Idumu-Oba.” At the compound where Eze lived, a neighbour said his wife was taken away on the day news of the killing reached them. “We don’t know anything about it. We were here when they sent the information to us, and even on the same day, they took her (Oyibo’s pregnant wife) away. “Personally, I was surprised when I heard the news. I never had any complaints from anybody that he had a problem with them. item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap: Tinubu donates N250m to victims’ families, as Shettima visits survivors
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has called for stricter enforcement of safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways following the tragic boat mishap in Bayelsa State, announcing a N250 million Federal Government donation to support the bereaved families. ‎ ‎He also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, vowing that the Federal Government would work with relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen vessel inspections, safety compliance and enforcement to prevent further loss of lives. ‎ ‎Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position on Sunday during a condolence visit to Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, following Friday’s boat accident at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. ‎ ‎Speaking at Government House, Yenagoa, the Vice President said the tragedy had exposed the urgent need to improve safety on inland waterways, particularly in riverine communities where water transportation remains essential to everyday life. ‎ ‎”We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima said preliminary reports suggesting that the boat developed a mechanical fault must be thoroughly investigated to establish the circumstances of the accident and identify possible failures in safety procedures. ‎ ‎”We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence. ‎ ‎”President Tinubu’s administration will continue working with the relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement on our inland waterways. The lives of our people are too precious for safety to remain an afterthought,” the Vice President stated. ‎ ‎Expressing grief over the tragedy, VP Shettima described the loss as particularly painful because the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony when the accident occurred. ‎ ‎”There is a particular cruelty in the tragedy that has brought us here today. item.title: ECOWAS Monetary Union: Cardoso advocates equity, fairness in governance structure
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, has called for equity, fairness and proportional representation in the governance structure of the proposed ECOWAS Monetary Union. He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the sovereign equality of member states must remain fundamental principles of the Union, these should be appropriately balanced with the relative financial commitments, responsibilities and risks borne by individual member states, particularly in determining participation in decision-making and governance. Cardoso made the call on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, on behalf of Nigeria at the Ministerial Session of the 6th Presidential Task Force Meeting on the ECOWAS Single Currency Programme in Abidjan, Cote d’ Ivoire. The Ministerial Committee of the ECOWAS Presidential Task Force comprises Ministers of Finance and Governors of central banks of PTF member states. He described the meeting as a defining milestone in the ECOWAS monetary integration process, noting that deliberations had recently focused on critical considerations regarding the institutional architecture of the proposed Monetary Union, including the location of its institutions, leadership appointments, and the allocation of authority and responsibilities. “The decisions we take today will shape the future of the Union for decades to come,” Cardoso told delegates. “They will influence its credibility in the eyes of investors and development partners, its legitimacy in the eyes of our citizens, and the confidence of Member States that their commitments are being matched by a meaningful voice within the institutions they are helping to build.” He restated Nigeria’s commitment to the ECOWAS Monetary Cooperation Programme and to establishing the ECO, describing it as “longstanding and unwavering” and citing substantial financial contributions, sustained technical support, and compromises made “in the broader interest of regional consensus”. “Nigeria has and will continue to demonstrate solidarity and fairness, respecting the sovereignty of other member states. We remain fully committed to the successful establishment of the ECO and to a Monetary Union that is credible, sustainable and beneficial to all Member States,” Cardoso declared. He, however, maintained that solidarity must be accompanied by equity, arguing that countries with larger economies and greater financial responsibilities should be given fair consideration in the governance of the institutions they support. “While bigger economies continue to take up the burden, they should also be considered to play a significant role because of the risk and systemic importance they have in the sub-region. Above all, such economies need to defend the huge contribution they make before their respective parliaments and the civil society. item.title: Tinubu has approved N450bn for farmers – APC-PCC
item.description: •Commits N1.5tr recapitalisation to BoA By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, said, yesterday, President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture, BoA, and committed N450 billion to agricultural financing programmes. The council said the commitment was meant “to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.” In a statement issued by the spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the bank had reached “over 500,000 smallholder farmers.” It added that the President “also approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.” According to the statement, the federal government “went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.” On the recapitalisation, the council, which noted that it was a major campaign promise of the President in 2023, said the move was designed “to enhance the bank’s financial capacity and ability to provide more affordable and accessible funding to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators, and other businesses operating across the agricultural value chain.” The statement added: “Under President Tinubu, a stronger Bank of Agriculture would be better positioned to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its reach to underserved farming communities, and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.” The council disclosed that the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, which had a programme value of N250 billion, financed farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies. These companies, it said, “coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.” The programme, according to the statement, has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women. It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds. The council said the programme targets two million farmers and the distribution of more than 10 million bags of fertiliser. It named Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi among the states receiving attention under the scheme. To shield farmers from price shocks, the statement said, the bank is implementing a N200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme. item.title: 2027: How we plan to present a common front — ADC, APM, NDC, SDP
item.description: By Dapo Akinrefon, Henry Umoru & Luminous Jannamike LAGOS — AHEAD of the 2027 general elections, major opposition parties have pledged to present a common front to wrest power from the All Progressives Congress, APC. The opposition parties that have indicated interest in the initiative include African Democratic Congress, ADC; Allied People’s Movement, APM; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC; and Social Democratic Party, SDP. Vanguard gathered that the parties are working in synergy with a view to presenting a common front to challenge the APC. Recall that presidential candidates of opposition parties, including Atiku Abubakar of the ADC, Peter Obi of the NDC, and Seyi Makinde of the APM, were scheduled to meet today to sign a Covenant for Democratic Renewal. However, they rescheduled their second summit to Monday, November 30, 2026, and agreed to suspend nationwide campaign activities on that day to enable party leaders and presidential candidates attend. Atiku exploring ways to reach power-sharing arrangement — ADC source Speaking on plans to present a common front, multiple sources close to the ADC presidential candidate told Vanguard that Atiku and the party were exploring ways to reach a power-sharing arrangement with other opposition parties. One of the sources said: “The party and the candidate are exploring ways in which opposition can work together in multiple areas, including ensuring violence-free campaigns, free and fair elections, making sure that the APC does not exert pressure on state institutions to alter election results and, of course, the possibility of consolidating the opposition through a power-sharing arrangement.” We’ll collaborate with progressive-minded parties, says NDC On how opposition parties plan to present a common front, the National Publicity Secretary of the NDC, Mr Osa Director, said the party supports opposition parties rallying around a single ticket. Mr Director said: “We have always appreciated what the G100 and other patriots are doing. “The NDC is willing to collaborate with any and all progressive-minded political party to rescue Nigeria from the suffocation of the ruling APC. Hence, we are presenting Nigerians with the best pair on the ballot, Obi/Kwankwaso ticket. Therefore, we are soliciting the support of all opposition parties to rally round the ticket.” We’re on the same page, says SDP Throwing his weight behind the initiative, the SDP’s National Publicity Secretary, Araba Rufus Aiyenigba, said the purpose of presenting a common front was to safeguard the country’s democracy. item.title: Tourist accuses Daura Emir of sexual assault
item.description: From Ibrahim Musa Giginyu, Katsina & Abdulyassar Abdulhamid, Abuja The Emir of Daura, His Royal Highness Alhaji Faruq Umar-Faruk, has been embroiled in an alleged sexual assault of a foreign tourist who visited his palace in Daura, Katsina State, during her tour of Nigeria. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, alleged in a viral video that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. When contacted, the Daura Emirate spokesperson (Sarkin Labarai), Ibrahim Murtala, confirmed that the Emirate has seen the video and they are currently analyzing its content, adding that the Emirate will address the matter after the conclusion of the ongoing processes. As of the time of filing this report, the state government had not issued any statement on the alleged sexual assault by the monarch. Attempts to reach the state Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Alhaji Bashir Tanimu, to comment on the matter failed as calls put through to his mobile phone were unanswered. He did not respond to a text message sent to him either. The Katsina State Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu, said the command was not aware of the video and did not receive any formal complaint from anyone on the matter. Describing the alleged experience, the tourist said she found it disgusting and had continued to think about what happened. She explained that although the incident occurred on November 14, she chose not to make it public until she had completed her Nigerian tour and left the country. In a post shared on her Instagram page alongside the video, the tourist wrote: “Recently I finished 30 days journey exploring all around #Nigeria. I had amazing time, saw beautiful places, met great people. “Unfortunately I had also a bad experience when visiting #daura in Northern Nigeria. During visit to the #emirofdaura palace I was taken to an elegant room where we sat on a couch and started talking. It was strange for me that he grabbed my hand and started playing with it. “Then when we stood up, he hugged me, kissed my cheek (which was also surprising for me), and then he grabbed my boobs. That was a shock for me. I told him “emir no, no, no, no” “emir you cannot be touching”, but he was just laughing about it. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way.” The tourist also suggested that she might not have been the first woman to experience such conduct from the Emir. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. item.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. item.title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
item.description: *Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG By Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic. They lamented that Nigerians have invested heavily in building rice mills but the government has failed to sustain the agricultural production policy needed to keep them running. item.title: Bears return to stock market as investors lose N2.9trn
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The stock market was characterised by massive sell off of shares last week, as investors lost over N2.9 trillion of their investments listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX. As the market traded on a bearish note, the NGX market capitalisation declined to N160.803 trillion from NI63.795 trillion the previous week. Similarly, another major performance indicator, NGX All Share Index, ASI dropped by 1.8 % to close at 247,660.74 points from 252,269.16 points the previous week. This is caused by sell pressure, which led to the fall in the price of Dangote Cement by -10.0%. It is followed by ARADEL, which lost -10.0%, Zenith Bank – 4.7% and GTCO -4.4%. Consequently, the Month-to-Date, MtD, and Year-to-Date, YtD, returns settled lower at -2.6% and +59.2%, respectively. On market activity, trading volume and value declined by 70.5% Week-on-Week, W/W and 42.6% W/W, respectively. Reacting to market outlook, Investors at Cordros Capital said: “ Looking ahead, we expect market activity to remain choppy and largely range-bound in the near term, as the absence of a clear catalyst continues to limit buying interest.” Also reacting to market performance and outlook, investors at InvestData Consulting Limited, said : “Persistent selling pressure and a failure to hold the 248,000-point support zone could expose the market to additional downside, particularly if institutional investors continue to lock in profits. However, continued profit-taking in recently appreciated equities could limit market recovery. Investors should focus on corporate earnings, dividend prospects, liquidity and valuation rather than short-term price movements.” Vanguard News The post Bears return to stock market as investors lose N2.9trn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Climate talks collapse in chaotic end to COP31
item.description: Climate advocates reacted with indignation on Monday to the COP31 summit ending in failure, with contentious talks collapsing over fossil fuels after the meeting in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected on Sunday in a chaotic finale to the UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. Calls for reform Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the summit with Turkey, attributed the failure of the talks to “difficult geopolitical times”. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”. The COP process is “in need of significant reform”, Gore said on X, as most countries sought “to move forward in good faith.” Falling short The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate dipl

item.title: COP31: Onuigbo tasks legislators on climate laws, funding
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The President of GLOBE Legislators International, Rt. Hon. Sir Sam Ifeanyi Onuigbo, has urged parliamentarians across the world to translate international climate agreements into enforceable national laws, backed by adequate funding and effective oversight. Onuigbo said international climate agreements would achieve little unless national parliaments incorporated decisions reached at United Nations climate conferences into domestic legislation and ensured their implementation. He made the call at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) COP31 Parliamentary Meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, where he highlighted the role of legislators in ensuring that commitments reached at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conferences of the Parties (COPs) produced tangible results at the national level. In a statement made available to journalists in Gombe on Saturday, the former member of the House of Representatives said parliamentarians must deploy their constitutional powers of lawmaking, budgetary appropriation and oversight to ensure governments implement international climate commitments. Drawing on his legislative experience, Onuigbo recalled that his participation in the GLOBE COP21 Legislators Summit in Paris influenced his decision to sponsor Nigeria’s Climate Change Act. He argued that without the necessary legislative backing, negotiations and agreements reached at international climate conferences could fail to translate into practical outcomes. “After all the contributions here, if they are not brought down into laws for implementation, it becomes an exercise in futility,” he said. Onuigbo described parliamentary action as central to bridging the gap between international climate negotiations and domestic implementation. He stressed that legislators must ensure that agreements reached at COP meetings were reflected in national laws, budgetary allocations and effective government oversight. Describing the deliberations at the Antalya meeting as detailed and incisive, he said their impact would ultimately depend on the ability of parliamentarians to translate the discussions into actionable legislation. The GLOBE Legislators president also commended the National Council on Climate Change, its leadership under Dr Majekodunmi, researchers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the development of the Host Country Approval Criteria for Carbon Market Activities in Nigeria and the country’s broader climate change efforts. He also acknowledged President Bola Tinubu’s role in Nigeria’s climate change efforts. “Above all, I want to thank President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who has exercised admirable leadership in ensuring that the climate journey remains steady and very successful,” he said. Onuigbo was inaugurated as President of GLOBE Legislators at the United Kingdom Parliament on June 24, 2026. item.title: Inuwa Yahaya pledges palace upgrade, flags off two roads
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has pledged to reconstruct and modernise the historic palace of the Mai Tula, Dr Abubakar Buba Atare, while flagging off two road projects in the traditional chiefdom. Yahaya made the pledge when he led the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign team on a royal visit to the Mai Tula’s palace, where he sought the monarch’s blessings and support for the party’s candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing the traditional ruler and members of his council, the governor said the visit was to acknowledge the role of traditional institutions in promoting peace, unity and community development. Yahaya, who holds the traditional title of Sodangin Tula, appreciated the people of the area for their reception and support for his administration, which he said had enabled him to serve the state for two consecutive terms. He urged the monarch and his subjects to sustain their support for the APC, particularly by voting for the party’s governorship candidate, Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, President Bola Tinubu and other candidates in the forthcoming elections. The governor expressed confidence that Gwamna would build on the development foundation laid by his administration and surpass its achievements, particularly in infrastructure and other critical sectors. On the palace renovation, Yahaya directed the Joint Projects Development and Essential Social Services Agency to ensure the immediate commencement of work, disclosing that the architectural design had already been submitted. He described the palace as an important historical monument, noting that it was built in the 1930s during the Native Authority era and deserved modernisation. “This is a historic palace built around the 1930s during the Native Authority era. It is high time we upgraded it into a modern palace comparable to those of other first-class traditional rulers across the state,” he said. Yahaya also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving rural connectivity through road infrastructure, recalling that the Yiri Road was constructed early in his tenure to improve access to the area. He subsequently flagged off the construction of the Wange-Baule and Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin roads, describing the projects as part of efforts to expand rural infrastructure and stimulate economic activities. The governor urged residents to support the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the State House of Assembly, arguing that political continuity would sustain development programmes and attract more projects to the area. Also speaking, the APC governorship candidate, Gwamna, promised to sustain and improve on the policies, programmes and projects of the Yahaya administration if elected. He acknowledged the importance of traditional rulers in maintaining peace and unity, urging the Mai Tula to use his influence to promote peaceful conduct before, during and after the 2027 general elections. item.title: MDGIF delivers 25 operational CNG stations in two years, backs 31 projects
item.description: By Uzoma Marvellous The Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) has supported the delivery of 25 operational Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) stations nationwide in two years, with its investment portfolio expanding to 31 projects comprising 205 infrastructure assets. The Executive Director of MDGIF, Mr. Oluwole Adama, disclosed this during the commissioning of CNG refueling facilities at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), University of Ibadan (UI), Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) and Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE), yesterday. He said the achievements reflected efforts by the Federal Government to deepen domestic gas utilisation, expand infrastructure and make natural gas more accessible to motorists and transport operators. “In just two years, MDGIF has supported the delivery of 25 fully operational CNG stations nationwide, bringing cleaner, more affordable fuel closer to motorists and transport operators,” Adama stated. Adama disclosed that the UNILAG facility was the 11th CNG station being commissioned in Lagos State, adding that nine additional university stations, mostly in Northern Nigeria, would be commissioned within weeks. “Eleven stations in one state is a clear signal that CNG is no longer a promise for tomorrow. In Lagos, it is becoming part of everyday life,” he said. Meanwhile, the Federal Government is expanding its university CNG initiative to 20 institutions, with 11 stations already commissioned under the programme. The Chief Executive Officer of Femadec Energy Limited, Engr. Fola Akinnola, said the company planned to complete six additional stations before the end of 2026, while the remaining three would be commissioned early in 2027. The programme began with facilities at the University of Abuja, Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and Federal University of Technology, Owerri. Four others were subsequently commissioned at the University of Uyo, University of Calabar, Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun, and University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus. Akinnola said the 20-campus initiative would reduce transportation costs for students, lecturers and other university employees while supporting cleaner energy adoption. “Campus communities are dynamic hubs of daily movement, where high transportation costs directly impact students, faculty and support staff alike. By systematically delivering this 20-campus network, we are providing immediate, practical relief—cutting campus transit fuel costs while significantly lowering carbon emissions,” he said. On his part, the Minister of Education, Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa, said the programme, known as the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation (Project SPROUT), was designed to address the high cost of commuting among students and university workers. “Through the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation, known as Project SPROUT, we are addressing one major concern students raise with us directly: the cost of getting to c

item.title: Umuahia to host Africa’s second int’l village after Kigali
item.description: …As Abia indigenes in Abuja endorse Otti for 2nd term, transfer PVCs home By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has announced plans to establish Africa’s second International Village in Umuahia, following the existing facility in Kigali, Rwanda, as part of efforts to attract international investment and strengthen the state’s economic prospects. Otti disclosed this at the 2026 Abia Day celebration organised by the Abia Development Organization, Abuja branch, at the Indoor Sports Hall of the Moshood Abiola Stadium, Abuja. The event, themed “Abia Ekulie La”, also witnessed the endorsement of the governor for a second term by Abia indigenes resident in Abuja, who said they had transferred their Permanent Voter Cards to the state ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The governor, who commended Abians in the Federal Capital Territory for their contributions to the development of the state through remittances, urged them to consider investing in Abia and relocating some of their businesses home. He said the increasing interest in the state had triggered pressure on the real estate sector, describing the development as a positive indication of renewed economic confidence. “For those of you looking for opportunities outside Abuja, you should look home. A lot of people are now coming home and there is pressure on real estate. It is a good problem to have,” Otti said. The governor disclosed that his administration had been working on a Diaspora City since last year, assuring that the project would provide opportunities for Abians living outside the state to invest and establish businesses at home. He, however, revealed that the government was also collaborating with international organisations to develop another city, which he described as the second International Village in Africa after Kigali. “We are also working on another city in liaison with international organisations. Just like what you have in Kigali—the only international village in Africa. The second one will be in Umuahia,” he said. Otti thanked the Abuja-based Abians for endorsing him for another term, saying the reception he had received during his ongoing engagements across the state indicated that many residents were satisfied with his performance. In his keynote address, Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe, representing Abia South Senatorial District, said the state was gradually overcoming years of developmental setbacks under Otti’s leadership. Abaribe, who spoke on “Abia Ekulie La (Abia Has Risen): The Role of Good Governance,” said the governor’s administration had begun reconnecting the state with the aspirations of its founding fathers through investments in infrastructure, healthcare, education, human capital development and economic revitalisation. He said Abia had, for decades, struggled with the paradox of abundant potentials but poor development outcomes due to the absence of visionary leadership backed by clear plans. item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. item.title: Tinubu Urges APC Leaders To Unite Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has called on leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to reconcile their differences ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscoring the virtue of forgiveness. He made the call on Sunday at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family in Lagos State, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation. His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, and former defence minister, Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke. ﻿ While reacting to reports of a misunderstanding between Governor Dikko Radda and Masari in Katsina State, Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor. “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile with them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said. He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State. President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections. He thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria. ‘Obstacles Were On Our Way’ He also thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles which he said “were on our way”. “People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no ₦5 in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. “We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. “It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he was quoted as saying. He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said. “We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised. He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians. item.title: New Manager, Same Problems, Liverpool Thrash 10-Man Man Utd In Pochettino’s First Match
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. Manchester United’s Argentinian head coach Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time.
